sentences.span: US diesel and gasoline inventories are at the lowest levels in 15 years [17989]; The average price for a gallon of diesel was $6.52 Wednesday, up 91 cents from a month ago [18186]; President Trump floated a 90-day ban on diesel exports to help ease prices, although the White House later ruled out a flat ban [18186]; White House is preparing plan for 90-day diesel exports ban [18126]
sentences.why: The 15-year-low inventory figure and the $6.52/91-cent diesel price figure are both fully supported. But the export-ban clause is contradicted within the source set: Goldman's own Market Monitor (18186), covering the same week, states the White House 'later ruled out a flat ban' after Trump floated it, while a separate non-bank wrap-up (18126) headlines it as still 'preparing.' Presenting 'is preparing a 90-day ban' as settled fact, when a source in the set says the proposal was already rejected, is a status distortion (a floated-then-rejected conditional presented as an ongoing asserted plan).
